texts.setting.bios.about: 'disabled' starts the cartridge at once, through Virtual Jaguar's own replacement for the console's start-up (most games run so). 'enabled' runs the console's real boot ROM first, with its spinning cube, as the console does. The boot ROMs are built into the core. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.bios_type.about: Which of the console's boot ROMs, when Boot is 'enabled': 'k' is the Series K (the usual one), 'm' the Model M. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.cd_bios_type.about: Which CD BIOS, when CD Boot is 'bios': 'retail', the one the console was sold with, or 'dev', the developers' one (it starts developers' discs only). Only for the Jaguar CD. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.cd_boot_mode.about: How the Jaguar CD starts a disc: 'hle' through Virtual Jaguar's replacement for the CD's start-up (at once); 'bios' through the console's own CD BIOS, with its start-up animation, which also needs the boot ROM; 'auto' lets Virtual Jaguar choose by the disc. Only for the Jaguar CD. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.cd_read_speed.about: How fast the replacement start-up reads the disc ('2x' is the drive's own speed). Only for the Jaguar CD with CD Boot 'hle'. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.internal_resolution.about: '2x' draws the 3D of the games that use the blitter for it at twice the size, sharper. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.machine.about: 'jaguar' is the console with a cartridge. 'jaguarcd' is the console with the Jaguar CD on top, for the games on CD: a .cue with its track files, a .chd or a .cdi. The CD's start-up is Virtual Jaguar's replacement; nothing has to be supplied. Everything else depends on it, so changing it restarts the core.
texts.setting.p1_device.about: What is plugged into port 1: a pad (P1), a Team Tap with four pads (P1, P3, P4, P5), the Tempest 2000 rotary (P1's wheel and buttons), an analog joystick or a driving controller (P1's stick, hat and A to D), the early boards' paddle input (P1's stick and pad), a 6D controller (six axes and A to G), or a light gun (P1 Gun X, Gun Y and its buttons; Gun X and Y are a fraction of the picture, as Chimera makes of the mouse's place). It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.p2_device.about: What is plugged into port 2: a pad (P2), a Team Tap with four pads (P2, P6, P7, P8), the rotary, a mouse (P2 Mouse X and Y, how far it moves in a frame, and its two buttons) through the ST adapter, an Amiga mouse through the ST adapter, or through the Amiga adapter, an analog joystick, a driving controller, the paddle input or a 6D controller. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.pal.about: 'enabled' makes a PAL console (50 frames a second, as the European ones); 'disabled' an NTSC one (60). It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.risc_idle_skip.about: Whether the graphics and sound processors' waiting loops are skipped in one step, as Virtual Jaguar does by default. It makes the core faster. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.true_color.about: 'enabled' draws smooth shading with more colours than the console's own format. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.usefastblitter.about: 'enabled' uses Virtual Jaguar's faster and less exact blitter. 'disabled' is the exact one. It is part of the machine, so a movie needs the same value.
texts.setting.widescreen.about: 'enabled' stretches the picture to 16:9. It changes the picture only.
texts.slot.cart.help: The game's cartridge: a .j64 or .rom file (or .jag, .abs, .cof, .bin for homebrew).
texts.slot.disc.help: The game's Jaguar CD: a .cue file with the track files it names beside it, a .chd file, or a .cdi file.
texts.slot.savedata.help: What the machine's save memory holds at the start, for a project that begins from a saved game: a file as Emulator > Export Save Data... writes it (jaguar.eeprom for a cartridge, jaguarcd.memtrack for the CD, which holds the Memory Track's saves), or a RetroArch .srm. The file is never changed. Leave this empty to start with an empty save memory.
texts.slot.savedata.name_help: a save file is identified by its extension, .eeprom, .memtrack, .srm or .sav.
